mainTopic: The צִיץ verses for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and the dispute over sprinkling the separated כהנים: whether הזאה is compared to טבילה
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a קל וחומר: if the כהן גדול may never take his mind off the צִיץ, which has God's name once, then all the more so a person may not take his mind off his תפילין, which have it many times. The גמרא then works through how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the צִיץ verses. רבי יהודה says the צִיץ is מרצה only while it is worn. רבי שמעון says it is always מרצה, but only if it is whole and fit for the forehead, so a broken צִיץ does not work. Next the גמרא tries to link this dispute to a ברייתא about sprinkling the כהן גדול and the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה during their seven days of separation. רבי מאיר sprinkles every day, רבי יוסי only on the third and seventh days, and רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים splits the two cases. Two proposed reasons are rejected: טומאה דחויה versus הותרה, and whether טבילה בזמנה מצוה. The final answer is that רבי מאיר compares הזאה to טבילה and רבי יוסי does not. רבי חנינא does not compare them; the daily sprinkling for the כהן of the פרה is only an extra stringency (מעלה). The עמוד ends by starting to quote a ברייתא that lists the only difference between the two כהנים, and that ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the logical argument from the frontplate to תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The צִיץ has only one mention of God's name, and the כהן גדול may not take his mind off it. תפילין have many mentions of God's name, so this applies to them all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The צִיץ has only one mention of God's name, yet the תורה said it must be 'on his forehead always,' meaning he must not take his mind off it. תפילין have many mentions of God's name, so all the more so one must not take his mind off them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a קל וחומר: one may not stop paying attention to one's תפילין, just as the כהן גדול may not stop paying attention to his צִיץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תמיד in the צִיץ verse is read as 'constant awareness,' so the wearer must not be distracted from it. The more names of God an object carries, the stricter this awareness requirement should be. תפילין carry many names of God, so the rule applies to them even more strongly.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold frontplate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead, engraved with God's name
A mention of God's name
Taking one's mind off something; distraction
All the more so (the closing formula of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the הלכה that a person must stay aware of his תפילין while wearing them.

phrases.english: Just as the frontplate, which has on it
phrases.notes: The opening 'ומה' signals the first half of a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: only one mention of God's name,
the Torah said: 'upon his forehead always' —
meaning that he should not take his mind off it.
tefillin, which have many mentions of God's name —
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה צִיץ, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא אַזְכָּרָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a קל וחומר begun on the previous עמוד, which reads תמיד as a requirement of constant awareness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must not be distracted from one's תפילין, learned by קל וחומר from the צִיץ.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי שמעון from 'on his forehead … and he shall bear'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads תמיד as 'always מרצה.' The גמרא objects that the verse says 'על מצחו... ונשא,' which seems to tie acceptance to the צִיץ being on the forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, who says the צִיץ is always מרצה, isn't it written 'on his forehead... and he shall bear [the sin]'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's view with a verse that seems to link acceptance to wearing the צִיץ on the forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that the צִיץ brings acceptance even when it is not being worn. But the verse mentions 'his forehead' together with 'bearing' the sin. That sounds like acceptance works only when the צִיץ is on his forehead, which is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings acceptance; makes certain impure offerings acceptable
But isn't it written? (opening of a challenge from a פסוק)
'And he shall bear' — the צִיץ 'bears' the sin of impure offerings

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who says 'always' means it always effects acceptance,
but isn't it written: 'on his forehead … and he shall bear'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר תָּמִיד מְרַצֶּה, וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's reading of תמיד (awareness) to a challenge against רבי שמעון's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that the צִיץ is מרצה even when it is not on the forehead.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse joins 'his forehead' with 'bearing' the sin, which implies acceptance depends on the צִיץ being worn.

steps.title: That phrase only tells us where the frontplate goes
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, 'על מצחו... ונשא' only sets the place where the צִיץ is worn. It is not a condition for acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes only to set the place for the צִיץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון: the verse tells us where to place the צִיץ, not when it is מרצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on his forehead' are read as an instruction about location. Once they are read that way, they no longer say anything about when acceptance happens. That leaves רבי שמעון's 'always מרצה' intact.

keyTerms.meaning: To set its proper place
That is what it comes to teach

phrases.english: That verse is to set its place —
that is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לִקְבּוֹעַ לוֹ מָקוֹם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על מצחו ונשא' makes acceptance depend on wearing the צִיץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only fixes where the צִיץ is placed.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the frontplate's placement?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses 'על מצחו ונשא' for his acceptance rule. So where does he learn where the צִיץ is placed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה — from where does he learn the place of the צִיץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יהודה and asks for his source for the placement rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already uses 'על מצחו ונשא' to teach that the צִיץ is מרצה only when worn. That phrase is therefore not free for him to teach placement. The גמרא wants to know which verse he uses instead.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda — setting its place,
from where does he derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִקְבּוֹעַ לוֹ מָקוֹם מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up step 3 by asking how the other side learns the same placement rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for where the צִיץ is placed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from the other 'on his forehead'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns placement from the separate phrase 'על מצחו' in 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'on his forehead' (in 'and it shall be on his forehead always').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה has a second 'על מצחו' in the פסוק, and he uses it for placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'his forehead' twice. רבי יהודה uses one mention ('ונשא') for acceptance and the other ('והיה על מצחו תמיד') for placement. Each phrase has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate 'על מצחו' phrases in the פסוק. 'על מצחו ונשא' is one; 'והיה על מצחו תמיד' is the other. Here רבי יהודה uses the second one.

phrases.english: He derives it from 'on his forehead.'
phrases.notes: This is the 'על מצחו' in 'והיה על מצחו תמיד'.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵעַל מִצְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placement is learned from 'על מצחו' in 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.'

steps.title: Then רבי שמעון should also use that phrase for placement
steps.stepSummary: If that phrase teaches placement, רבי שמעון should learn placement from it too. That would leave 'ונשא' unexplained.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון too — let him learn it from 'on his forehead'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 3: why would רבי שמעון need 'ונשא' for placement if the other phrase already teaches it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placement is already available from 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.' If רבי שמעון also learns placement from there, his explanation of 'על מצחו ונשא' becomes unnecessary. The phrase is then left without a purpose in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from somewhere else)
Also; too

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon too,
let him derive it from 'on his forehead'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי, תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's source from step 5 to undermine רבי שמעון's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 3, that 'על מצחו ונשא' teaches placement for רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placement already comes from the other 'על מצחו,' so this phrase would be redundant.

steps.title: Agreed — רבי שמעון learns placement from there too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that רבי שמעון also learns placement from 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and drops the answer from step 3. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The placement explanation of 'ונשא' is withdrawn for רבי שמעון. The core מחלוקת is not affected. A new question now opens: what does רבי שמעון learn from 'ונשא'?

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (a concession)

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the point raised in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון does learn placement from 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.'

steps.title: So what does רבי שמעון learn from 'on his forehead … and he shall bear'?
steps.stepSummary: After the concession, the גמרא asks what purpose 'על מצחו ונשא' serves for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does he do with 'on his forehead... and he shall bear'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this phrase teaches according to רבי שמעון. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase can no longer teach placement for רבי שמעון, because that comes from elsewhere. It also cannot mean what רבי יהודה says, that acceptance requires wearing the צִיץ. The גמרא needs a new purpose for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

phrases.english: Rather, 'on his forehead … and he shall bear' —
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, עַל מִצְחוֹ וְנָשָׂא מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the concession in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון learns from 'על מצחו ונשא.'

steps.title: Only a frontplate fit for the forehead brings acceptance
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, the phrase teaches that the צִיץ must be fit to be worn on the forehead. A broken צִיץ is not מרצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: a צִיץ fit for the forehead is מרצה; one not fit for the forehead is not מרצה. This excludes a broken צִיץ, which is not מרצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון a new reading: the phrase requires the צִיץ to be wearable, so a broken צִיץ does not bring acceptance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads 'on his forehead' as describing the kind of צִיץ that works: one fit to be worn. He does not read it as describing when it works. So the צִיץ need not actually be on his head, but it must be whole and wearable.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be worn on the forehead
To exclude
Broken

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the צִיץ is מרצה only while worn. רבי שמעון: it is always מרצה, but only if it is whole and fit for the forehead; a broken צִיץ is not מרצה. Both learn placement from 'והיה על מצחו תמיד.'
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not require the צִיץ to be worn. He requires it to be wearable. 'Fit for the forehead' is not the same as 'on the forehead.'

phrases.english: He would say to you: one fit for the forehead effects acceptance;
one not fit for the forehead does not effect acceptance.
This excludes a case where the frontplate broke,
in which case it does not effect acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: רָאוּי לַמֵּצַח מְרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase requires a צִיץ fit for the forehead, which excludes a broken צִיץ.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבי שמעון's view, the צִיץ is מרצה even when it is not being worn, but not if it is broken.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the broken צִיץ rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון used 'על מצחו ונשא' to teach that a broken צִיץ is not מרצה. רבי יהודה needs those words to teach that the צִיץ is מרצה only while worn, so where does he get the broken צִיץ rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, where does he learn the rule that a broken צִיץ does not work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה gets the rule that a broken צִיץ is not מרצה. The verse that רבי שמעון used for this rule is already taken by רבי יהודה for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי שמעון used 'על מצחו ונשא' to teach that the צִיץ must be fit to be worn, so a broken one does not work. But רבי יהודה uses 'על מצחו ונשא' to teach that the צִיץ is מרצה only while it is actually on the forehead (Step 2), and he learns placement from the other 'על מצחו' (Step 5). So the גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's source for the broken צִיץ rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The צִיץ broke
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda,
a broken frontplate (that it does not work), from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, נִשְׁבַּר הַצִּיץ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the source question from רבי שמעון to רבי יהודה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source רבי יהודה uses for the rule that a broken צִיץ is not מרצה

steps.title: He learns it from 'his forehead' instead of 'forehead'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the broken צִיץ rule from the extra word-form 'מצחו'. רבי שמעון does not learn from this difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the fact that the Torah wrote 'his forehead' and not just 'forehead.' And רבי שמעון does not learn anything from 'forehead' versus 'his forehead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה learns the rule from the Torah saying 'מצחו' (his forehead) rather than 'מצח' (forehead). It also explains why רבי שמעון needed a different source: he does not read anything into this word difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His forehead' suggests the צִיץ must be something fit to sit on the כהן גדול's forehead, and a broken צִיץ is not fit. רבי שמעון does not treat that small word difference as meaningful. That is why he needed the words 'על מצחו ונשא' for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it
'Forehead' versus 'his forehead'
He does not find meaning in it; he does not learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a broken צִיץ is not מרצה. They only disagree about which words in the פסוק teach it.

phrases.english: He derives it from (the Torah writing) 'his forehead' rather than 'forehead.'
And Rabbi Shimon does not learn anything from 'forehead' versus 'his forehead.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״מֵּצַח״ ״מִצְחוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה derives the rule from 'מצחו' rather than 'מצח'. רבי שמעון does not derive from this difference.

steps.title: Suggesting this dispute matches another dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is the same as a dispute found in a בָּרַיְיתָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that these תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by suggesting a comparison. This line is a setup: the next step quotes the בָּרַיְיתָא being compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'These תנאים' are רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, whose dispute connects to impurity in public offerings. 'Those תנאים' are רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי in the upcoming בָּרַיְיתָא. The גמרא wants to see whether both pairs are really arguing about the same underlying idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
These תנאים are like those תנאים (the two disputes are the same)

phrases.english: Shall we say that these tanna'im are like those tanna'im?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the source discussion ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון matches the dispute in the following בָּרַיְיתָא

steps.title: The בָּרַיְיתָא on sprinkling the separated כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Before their service, the כהן גדול and the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה are separated for seven days. Three opinions disagree on which days we sprinkle מי חטאת on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: For both this one (the כהן גדול before יום הכיפורים) and that one (the כהן who burns the פרה), we sprinkle on him all seven days from all the חטאות that were there. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: we sprinkle on him only on the third and seventh days. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says: the כהן who burns the פרה gets sprinkled all seven days, but the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים only on the third and seventh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the בָּרַיְיתָא it wants to compare. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will try to explain the reasoning behind the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is טמא מת becomes pure through sprinkling on the third and seventh days. We do not know if or when these כהנים may have become טמא. רבי מאיר therefore sprinkles every day, so that the right days are always covered. רבי יוסי sprinkles only on days three and seven of the separation. רבי חנינא splits the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a בָּרַיְיתָא
We sprinkle on him (purifying water with פרה אדומה ashes)
The ashes of the פרות אדומות, which the Torah calls חטאת
The third and seventh days, the days of purification from טומאת מת
The deputy כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'חטאות' here does not mean sin-offering animals. It means the ashes of earlier פרות אדומות that were stored in the מקדש.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Both this one and that one
we sprinkle upon him all seven days
from all the red-heifer ashes that were there
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַזִּין עָלָיו אֶלָּא שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: We sprinkle upon him only on the third and seventh days alone.
Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest, says:
The priest who burns the heifer
we sprinkle upon him all seven days;
the High Priest on Yom Kippur

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַזִּין עָלָיו אֶלָּא שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי.
phrases.english: we sprinkle upon him only on the third and seventh days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מַזִּין עָלָיו כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the בָּרַיְיתָא referenced in the comparison
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: sprinkle all seven days on both כהנים. רבי יוסי: only on the third and seventh. רבי חנינא: all seven for the פרה כהן, only the third and seventh for the כהן גדול.

steps.title: Proposed reason: דחויה versus הותרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds טומאה דחויה בציבור and רבי יוסי holds טומאה הותרה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? רבי מאיר holds that impurity is only 'pushed aside' (דחויה) for the public. And רבי יוסי holds that impurity is fully 'permitted' (הותרה) for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind the רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי dispute. If this reason holds, it would match the רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דחויה' means the ban on serving while טמא still exists; it is only pushed aside when needed, so we should still try hard to be pure. That would explain רבי מאיר's extra sprinkling every day. 'הותרה' means impurity is completely allowed for public offerings, which seems to explain why רבי יוסי is more relaxed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (a proposed explanation)
They disagree
For the public, the ban on impurity is pushed aside but still exists
For the public, impurity is fully permitted

steps.confusionAlert: דחויה and הותרה both allow a public offering in טומאה when there is no choice. The difference is whether we must still try to avoid טומאה (דחויה) or need not bother at all (הותרה).

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they disagree?
Rabbi Meir holds:
Impurity is (only) overridden in public matters.
And Rabbi Yosei holds:
Impurity is permitted in public matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the בָּרַיְיתָא in a way that would support the comparison
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about דחויה versus הותרה

steps.title: If impurity were permitted, why sprinkle at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proposal. If רבי יוסי held הותרה, he would not require any sprinkling at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think so? If רבי יוסי held that impurity is permitted for the public, why do I need sprinkling at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it just suggested for רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי still requires sprinkling, so he cannot hold הותרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If impurity were fully permitted, there would be no reason to purify the כהן גדול at all. Yet רבי יוסי requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days. That shows he still treats impurity as something to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (introduces a rejection)
Sprinkling of purifying water
At all

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
If Rabbi Yosei holds
that it is permitted in public matters,
why do I need sprinkling at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? אִי סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֶיתֵּר הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of רבי יוסי's view proposed in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds טומאה הותרה בציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under הותרה no purification would be needed, but רבי יוסי does require sprinkling.

steps.title: Both תנאים hold impurity is only pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי both hold טומאה דחויה בציבור. So their dispute is not about דחויה versus הותרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone, these תנאים too, holds that impurity is only pushed aside for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its suggestion. Both תנאים in the בָּרַיְיתָא hold דחויה, so they cannot be the source for the דחויה/הותרה dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both require sprinkling, both must hold that impurity is only pushed aside. Their disagreement about how many days to sprinkle must come from some other issue. The proposed comparison to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון therefore falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They hold

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to link רבי מאיר/רבי יוסי with the דחויה/הותרה dispute is rejected. Both of them hold טומאה דחויה בציבור, since both require sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone, (all) these tanna'im,
hold that impurity is (only) overridden in public matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי סָבְרִי טוּמְאָה דְּחוּיָה הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 15 by rejecting the proposal of Step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the explanation that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about דחויה versus הותרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי requires sprinkling, which only makes sense if impurity is דחויה.

steps.title: A new explanation: the dispute is about immersing on time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds טבילה בזמנה מצוה and רבי יוסי does not. That would explain their different sprinkling schedules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is what they really disagree about. רבי מאיר holds that we say immersing at its proper time is a מצוה. רבי יוסי holds that we do not say immersing at its proper time is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 16 showed they are not arguing about דחויה versus הותרה. Now the גמרא offers a new reason for their argument: whether it is a מצוה to purify yourself at the earliest possible moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We worry the כהן may have become impure in the days before he was separated. So any day could be his 3rd or 7th day of impurity. רבי מאיר says purifying on time is a מצוה, so he sprinkles every day to be sure he hits the right day, while רבי יוסי says it is enough to sprinkle on the 3rd and 7th days of the separation.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה to become pure
At its proper time, the earliest moment it can be done
Here they disagree about this point
We say / we hold

phrases.english: And here they disagree about this:
Rabbi Meir holds:
We say that immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: So he sprinkles on the כהן every day, in case today is the right day.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
We do not say that immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: So sprinkling on the 3rd and 7th days of the separation is enough, even if purification comes late.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16 removed the דחויה/הותרה explanation, this step offers a new reason for the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about טומאה דחויה versus הותרה בציבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether טבילה בזמנה מצוה.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of ה׳'s name written on the skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי really rejects טבילה בזמנה מצוה. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי יוסי lets a person with ה׳'s name on his skin immerse right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that we do not say immersing on time is a מצוה? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone had ה׳'s name written on his skin, he may not bathe, may not smear oil, and may not stand in a dirty place. If he needs to do a מצוה immersion, he wraps a reed over the name and immerses. רבי יוסי says: he goes down and immerses normally, as long as he does not rub the spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from step 17. It brings a ברייתא to test what רבי יוסי really holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s name must be guarded from being erased or disgraced. The תנא קמא tells the person to cover the name with a reed before immersing, which may take time. רבי יוסי lets him immerse right away without covering it, and the next step explains why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
A name of ה׳
A reed, wrapped over the name to protect it
A dirty or filthy place
Rub, which could erase the name

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold
that we do not say immersion at its proper time is a מצוה?
But was it not taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה שֵׁם כָּתוּב עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ —
phrases.english: One who had a name of God written on his flesh,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִרְחַץ וְלֹא יָסוּךְ
phrases.english: he may not bathe, and may not smear oil,
and may not stand in a place of filth.
If a מצוה immersion came up for him,
he wraps a reed over it and immerses.
phrases.notes: The reed protects the name without blocking the water.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He goes down and immerses in his usual way,
as long as he does not rub.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא אָמְרִינַן טְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 17 that רבי יוסי rejects טבילה בזמנה מצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds we do not say טבילה בזמנה מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי letting someone immerse right away without stopping to cover ה׳'s name. That suggests he values immersing on time.

steps.title: The ברייתא's dispute is exactly about immersing on time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that it is known the ברייתא's dispute is about טבילה בזמנה מצוה. The תנא קמא rejects it and רבי יוסי accepts it, which is the opposite of step 17.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have an established rule that they disagree about whether immersing on time is a מצוה. The תנא קמא holds that we do not say immersing on time is a מצוה. רבי יוסי holds that we do say immersing on time is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It shows how the ברייתא proves that רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lets the person delay his immersion until he finds a reed, so for him immersing on time is not a מצוה. רבי יוסי says immerse now, without waiting, because immersing on time is a מצוה. This directly contradicts what step 17 said about רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is established for us / we know
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And we hold it established
that they disagree about whether immersion at its proper time is a מצוה:
The first tanna holds:
We do not say immersion at its proper time is a מצוה,
phrases.notes: So he may wait until he finds a reed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
We say immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: So he immerses immediately, without delay.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַיְימָא לַן דְּבִטְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 18 by explaining what the ברייתא's dispute is about.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה מצוה. So he cannot be the one who rejects it in our dispute.

steps.title: Retraction: all these תנאים agree that immersing on time is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the explanation from step 17. Both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי hold טבילה בזמנה מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone among these תנאים says that immersing on time is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and takes back its earlier explanation. This sets up a new explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה מצוה, both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree on it. Their argument about sprinkling must therefore come from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea)
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Rather, everyone among these tanna'im agrees
that we say immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of steps 18-19 and withdraws step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The explanation that the dispute is about טבילה בזמנה מצוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי clearly holds טבילה בזמנה מצוה in the ברייתא about ה׳'s name.

steps.title: The real dispute: is sprinkling compared to immersion?
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that טבילה בזמנה מצוה. רבי מאיר compares הזאה to טבילה, so sprinkling on time is also a מצוה. רבי יוסי does not compare them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here is what they disagree about. רבי מאיר holds that we compare sprinkling to immersion. רבי יוסי holds that we do not compare sprinkling to immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final explanation of the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about sprinkling the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the rule that טבילה should be done on time also applies to הזאה, so he sprinkles every day to catch the right day. For רבי יוסי, the rule applies only to immersion, so sprinkling on the 3rd and 7th days of the separation is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare / equate (one law to another)
Sprinkling the מי חטאת (ashes of the פרה אדומה mixed with water)

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: all agree that טבילה בזמנה מצוה. רבי מאיר compares הזאה to טבילה, so he sprinkles every day. רבי יוסי does not compare them, so he sprinkles only on the 3rd and 7th days.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two מצוות: טבילה is immersing in a מקוה, and הזאה is having the purifying water sprinkled on you. Everyone agrees about טבילה. The argument is only about whether הזאה follows the same rule.

phrases.english: And here they disagree about this:
Rabbi Meir holds:
We compare sprinkling to immersion,
phrases.notes: So sprinkling on time is also a מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
We do not compare sprinkling to immersion.
phrases.notes: Only immersion must be done on time, not sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: מַקְּשִׁינַן הַזָּאָה לִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 showed both agree on טבילה בזמנה מצוה, this step finds the real difference: whether הזאה is compared to טבילה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They disagree about whether טבילה בזמנה מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree about טבילה. They disagree about whether הזאה is compared to טבילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute about sprinkling the כהן depends on whether הזאה is compared to טבילה.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's split ruling seems inconsistent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים. Whether or not he compares הזאה to טבילה, he should treat the כהן who burns the פרה and the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים? If he compares sprinkling to immersion, then even the כהן on יום הכפורים should also be sprinkled every day. If he does not compare sprinkling to immersion, then even the כהן who burns the פרה should also not be sprinkled every day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a third opinion, רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים. It shows that his two rulings do not seem to fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained the disagreement with one idea: does הזאה follow the rules of טבילה or not? רבי חנינא treats the two כהנים differently. The פרה כהן is sprinkled all seven days, but the כהן גדול is not. Under either side of that one idea, the two cases should come out the same, so his split looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy to the כהן גדול
Compares one thing to another so that it shares its rules (a היקש)
Sprinkling of the purifying water mixed with the ashes of the פרה
Immersion in a מקוה
Also / too

steps.confusionAlert: This is a 'heads I win, tails you lose' challenge. The גמרא is not claiming רבי חנינא holds one side. It is saying that whichever side he holds, his split ruling does not work.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina the deputy of the priests — what does he hold?
If he compares sprinkling to immersion
then even the priest on Yom Kippur should also be sprinkled every day
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't actually say 'should be sprinkled every day,' but that's what it means here.

phrases.english: If he does not compare sprinkling to immersion

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: then even the priest who burns the heifer should also not be sprinkled every day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים? אִי מַקֵּישׁ הַזָּאָה לִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the framework from step 21 (comparing הזאה to טבילה) and applies it to a third תנא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's different sprinkling rules for the כהן of the פרה and the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a dilemma. Either he compares הזאה to טבילה or he does not. Either way, the two cases should be treated alike, so his split is unexplained.

steps.title: He does not compare them; the heifer priest is just an extra stringency
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא does not compare הזאה to טבילה. The seven days of sprinkling for the כהן who burns the פרה is only an added stringency (מעלה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, he does not compare sprinkling to immersion. The sprinkling of the כהן who burns the פרה every day is just an extra stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא holds like רבי יוסי. By the basic rule, neither כהן needs sprinkling every day. The פרה case is a special stringency added on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he does not compare הזאה to טבילה, the default is no daily sprinkling, and that explains the כהן גדול. The daily sprinkling for the פרה כהן does not come from the basic rule. It is a מעלה, an extra level of care that חכמים added for the פרה, which must be done in great purity.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth. It signals that the גמרא is going back to one side of the dilemma
An added stringency or higher standard set by חכמים
Merely / just

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים does not compare הזאה to טבילה. The daily sprinkling for the כהן of the פרה is only a rabbinic stringency (מעלה), not the basic rule.

phrases.english: Actually, he does not compare sprinkling to immersion
and as for the priest who burns the heifer
that is merely an added stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא מַקֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma in step 22 by choosing one side and explaining the other case as an exception
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma (no היקש) and explains the other case as an added stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Daily sprinkling for the פרה כהן seemed to show that רבי חנינא compares הזאה to טבילה
steps.terutzMaskana: He does not compare them. The daily sprinkling for the פרה is only a מעלה.

steps.title: Which תנא matches the ברייתא comparing the two כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the opinions above matches a ברייתא that lists the only difference between the כהן who burns the פרה and the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this ברייתא that the Rabbis taught: There is no difference between the כהן who burns the פרה and the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים except...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup step. The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא in order to find out which תנא it follows. The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The format 'אין בין... אלא' lists the only difference between two cases. Everything not listed is the same for both. The answer will depend on which difference the ברייתא names, so we have to wait for the rest of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does this go? (Which opinion does it match?)
The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא
There is no difference between... except. It lists the only distinction
The High Priest

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops at 'אלא'. The actual difference comes on the next עמוד, so do not try to answer the question yet.

phrases.english: According to whom does it go
this that the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה
phrases.english: There is no difference between the priest who burns the heifer
and the High Priest on Yom Kippur except...
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי, and רבי חנינא are explained, the גמרא tests which of them a ברייתא follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא (רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי, or רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים) the ברייתא comparing the two כהנים follows
